messages:
rahul_mobile: Running into flaky cancellation + duplicate-refresh issues in the sample app when using enqueue() from a BackgroundWorker. Happens most when the device is dozing and we run several small API calls in parallel.

sophia_sdk: Can you describe the flow? Is the Authenticator doing suspending work?

rahul_mobile: Flow: WorkManager -> BackgroundWorker -> in doWork() we call retrofitService.pushEvents().enqueue(...). If token expired, Authenticator starts token refresh which is suspending (Coroutine) and we do an in-memory cache check. Because enqueue doesn't propagate coroutine cancellation, when the app goes to background we get multiple simultaneous authenticator invocations.

ben_infra: Classic lifecycle gap. Enqueue is fire-and-forget; WorkManager threads can get starved/delayed on Doze and coroutines get cancelled elsewhere, so your in-memory guard loses consistency.

olga_qe: Repro? Is there a small sample branch?

rahul_mobile: Pushed a minimal repro: android/samples/bg-worker-enqueue-cancel-race. Logs show repeated: 
```
I/Auth: refresh started (req=5)
I/Auth: refresh started (req=6)
W/OkHttp: request failed, retrying
I/Network: 401 -> invoking authenticator
```

sophia_sdk: Two pragmatic options: (1) convert worker calls to suspending pattern using Call.await() so cancellation is propagated and you can use a Mutex or AtomicReference single-flight, (2) keep Authenticator sync: perform the token refresh in a blocking fashion inside Authenticator (so OkHttp serializes it), but be careful with blocking threads.

ben_infra: If you choose (1), implement Call.await() that cancels the underlying Call when coroutine is cancelled. Also persist token in DataStore so background workers read latest token and don't start redundant refreshes.

rahul_mobile: I prototyped an AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred<Token>> single-flight approach and switched worker to withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { service.pushEvents().await() }. That fixed duplicates but introduced long blocking during refresh on some older devices.

olga_qe: Did you also limit OkHttp Dispatcher concurrency? If many workers start at once they can overwhelm and trigger lots of queued requests that hit Authenticator concurrently. Try Dispatcher(maxRequests=6, maxRequestsPerHost=2).

rahul_mobile: Yes applying dispatcher limits + short callTimeout helped. Also added an exponential backoff for failed refreshes.

sophia_sdk: For onboarding, we should add a one-page guideline: "Android SDK: Background workers, enqueue() caveats, and Authenticator single-flight patterns" with sample code for: Call.await() adapter that ties cancel to Call.cancel(), an Authenticator snippet using AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred>, and recommended OkHttp defaults for mobile.

ben_infra: Agreed. Also add a CI emulator test that runs a few background workers with doze/network toggles to prevent regressions.

build-bot: CI: samples/bg-worker-enqueue-cancel-race build queued (job #8123).

rahul_mobile: Thanks — I'll open the doc PR and add the sample to the emulator matrix. Small ask: can someone review the Authenticator snippet before I merge?
